we have investigated the effects of hydrodynamic flow, thermal noise and the composition dependent bending modulus on the coarsenings of phase separated patterns on the surface of vesicles.
the composition dependent membrane bending rigidity plays an important role in the shape deformation and phase separation dynamics of two component liposomes.

(i) the dynamics of phase separated vesicles is influenced by the hydrodynamic flow induced from the line tension of a domain boundary, (ii) the dynamics of a bicontinuos phase separated vesicle is influenced by hydrodynamic flow, and (iii) the dynamics of shape fixed vesicles is influenced both by hydrodynamic flow and by the bending rigidity which depends on the composition in lipids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of two-component vesicles, which is important for understanding the biological function of the cell membranes.

the dynamics of phase separated patterns on the surfaces of two component vesicle and the dynamics of shape changes coupled with phase separation in two component vesicles with composition dependent bending rigidy.
the effects of thermal fluctuations, hydrodynamic flows and composition dependent bending rigidities on the phase separation and shape change of vesicles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dynamics of phase separation and deformation in vesicles are coupled and that the composition dependent membrane bending rigidity plays a crucial role in this coupling.
the coarsening and deformation of the phase separated vesicles are strongly influenced by the effects of thermal fluctuations, hydrodynamic flow and composition dependent bending rigidy.
the composition dependent rigidity of the vesicle membrane plays an important role in the dynamics of shape and phase separation of the membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coarsening process of the phase separated domains on the vesicle surface is influenced by the shape of vesicle and the composition dependent bending modulus of the membrane.

the dynamics of phase separation and vesicle shape deformation can be described in terms of a single parameter (the ratio of the bending rigidity to the line tension) which is determined by the composition of the lipid membrane.

the composition dependent properties of the lipid membrane such as the bending rigidity, the line tension and the surface tension are important to determine the dynamics of the vesicle and the domain pattern on the surface of the vesicle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the composition dependent membrane properties can lead to a rich dynamics of shape deformation and phase separation in vesicles.
the dynamics of shape change and phase separation in a two component vesicle is strongly influenced by the composition dependent bending rigidities of the membrane.

the coarsening process in a phase separated two-component vesicle is significantly influenced by hydrodynamic flow induced from the line tension of domain boundaries, thermal noise and the composition dependent bending rigidities.
